name: Everpure, Inc. (formerly Pure Storage)

profile.description: Everpure, Inc., the former Pure Storage, provides all-flash enterprise data storage (FlashArray, FlashBlade, DirectFlash) sold both as products and through its Evergreen subscription model. NOTE: the company now trades on the NYSE under the ticker P; the PSTG symbol no longer carries a current quote, and all market data in this report are for P [5]. Fiscal Q2 2027 (ended August 2, 2026) revenue was about $1.19B, up 38% year over year, as hyperscaler DirectFlash wins added to enterprise demand; product revenue grew 54% to $687M and subscription services revenue grew 20% to $499M [2][4]. CEO Charles Giancarlo, formerly Cisco's CTO, has led the company since August 2017 [8].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Over five years the company built the Evergreen subscription model (subscription services now 42% of revenue, $499M in Q2 FY27, +20%) and then opened a new hyperscaler channel for DirectFlash. That channel helped growth jump from 16% in FY2026 to 38% in Q2 FY27, with product revenue up 54% [1][2][4]. AI Deployment (2/2): FlashBlade and DirectFlash ship into AI training and inference data centers, and management credits hyperscaler and AI infrastructure demand for the growth acceleration [2][3]. Market Share (2/2): The company serves a majority of the Fortune 500 per its FY2026 release, and Q4 FY26 revenue topped $1B for the first time, +20% versus a low-growth storage market [1]. Product Pipeline (2/2): Management expects large hyperscaler DirectFlash order commitments to run into calendar 2028 and guides Q3 FY27 revenue to $1.325-$1.335B (~38% growth), with remaining performance obligations up 40% to $3.7B [1][2][4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): TTM R&D is 23.4% of revenue ($963M in FY2026), top quartile for storage hardware [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Everpure says it is 'committed to revolutionizing data storage and management' and simplifying how people access and use data. That states clearly what the company does but no deeper purpose beyond its category [5]. Community Impact (0/2): Our searches found ESG reporting built on three pillars (technology, operations, people) and claims about flash energy efficiency, but no foundation, dollar giving commitments, or distinctive community programs, and ESG reporting does not count as Inspiration evidence [9][10]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data are disclosed. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP data show zero open-market purchases and 86 open-market sales in Q3 2026 alone (2.69M shares disposed), plus 44 more sales in Q4 to date, which is heavy net insider selling into the rally [7].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 7 growth-sleeve metrics (10 weight units). The balance sheet is very strong: D/E is 14.6% and TTM ROE is 17.4%, both 1.0 (ROE at 2x weight) [5]. Revenue growth is 37.7% YoY in Q2 FY27 and the 5-year CAGR is 16.8% (FY2021 $1.68B to FY2026 $3.66B), both 1.0 [5]. The drags are valuation and GAAP profitability. The forward P/E of 33.1 is derived from a blend of FY2027/FY2028 consensus EPS of $2.78/$4.19 at $126.98 and scores 0.67 [6]. The TTM GAAP net margin of 5.9% scores 0.30 because of stock-based compensation, which is 9.2% of revenue [5]. FMP's reported forward PEG of 3.88 scores 0 at 2x weight; on non-GAAP consensus EPS growth of ~51% for FY2028, the implied PEG would be well under 1, so this metric is harsh [5][6]. Weighted sum 6.97/10 = 7. Liquidity is about 4.2M shares/day x $126.98 (~$534M daily).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Everpure is AI infrastructure. AI training and inference need large, fast, power-efficient storage, and hyperscalers are committing to DirectFlash with orders expected into calendar 2028, so AI raises demand rather than substituting for the product [2][3]. The main risks are cyclical, not substitution: NAND/memory pricing (some of the growth reflects price increases amid a memory shortage) and hyperscaler concentration [2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI-driven hyperscaler and enterprise demand drove Q2 FY27 product revenue up 54% to $687M and lifted FY27 revenue guidance to roughly $5B (~38% midpoint growth), up from $4.3-$4.4B in February [2][4].

infinite_game.summary: Viewed as Sinek would, Everpure has the bones of an enduring company: a leader in place since 2017, the Evergreen model that traded upfront revenue for lasting customer relationships, and a willingness to reach into hyperscale. But its stated purpose is a category description rather than a Just Cause, competitive language centers on displacing Dell, NetApp and HPE, and heavy insider selling does not signal a team playing for decades. It is a high-quality execution story more than an infinite-minded institution.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The purpose, revolutionizing data storage and simplifying data access, describes the product category rather than a future state worth sacrificing for [5]. The 2026 rebrand from Pure Storage to Everpure signals a broader data-platform ambition, but leadership commentary centers on revenue guidance and hyperscaler wins rather than a cause [2][4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Charles Giancarlo has led the company since August 2017, and the shift from founder-era leadership to his tenure was orderly, with prior CEO Scott Dietzen moving to chairman [8]. Our searches found no employee-sentiment or turnover data either way, so trust is rated adequate rather than high.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Public commentary frames competition as share capture from legacy disk and hybrid vendors and hyperscaler displacement of incumbents, a 'win the deal' posture. We found no evidence of management citing rivals' strengths as lessons [2][3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company moved from selling hardware boxes to Evergreen subscriptions (now 42% of revenue) and from enterprise-only to hyperscaler DirectFlash supply, then rebranded as Everpure [2][4]. These are significant evolutions of the same flash-storage franchise rather than abandoning a core business, so the score is 1.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Backing Evergreen subscriptions meant giving up upfront product revenue for ratable recurring revenue, and the company has kept R&D at about 23% of revenue ($963M in FY2026) while GAAP margins stayed in single digits [5]. Heavy and continuous insider selling (0 purchases versus 86 sales in Q3 2026) weakens the signal that leadership is sacrificing personally for the long game [7].

investment_thesis: Everpure is in a growth re-acceleration. FY2026 revenue reached $3.66B (+16%) with Q4 above $1B, and fiscal Q2 2027 revenue grew 38% to $1.19B as product revenue jumped 54% on hyperscaler DirectFlash demand [1][2][4]. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to about $5B (~38% midpoint growth) with operating profit of $940-$960M. Consensus EPS is expected to climb from $2.78 in FY2027 to $4.19 in FY2028, and the balance sheet carries net cash with D/E of only 14.6% [4][5][6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and durability. At $126.98 the stock trades at 167x TTM GAAP earnings, about 99x EV/EBITDA, and roughly 10x sales, with a GAAP net margin of only 5.9% and stock-based compensation at 9.2% of revenue [5]. Part of the acceleration reflects price increases during a memory shortage, and the shares fell after the Q2 beat. Any normalization of NAND pricing, delay in hyperscaler commitments, or heavier insider selling (130 open-market sales in Q3-Q4 2026) could compress the multiple sharply [2][7].
key_catalysts: Q3 FY27 results (expected late November 2026) against guidance of $1.325-$1.335B, ~38% growth, could confirm the hyperscaler ramp [4]
Hyperscaler DirectFlash order commitments that management expects to extend into calendar 2028 provide multi-year revenue visibility [2]
Remaining performance obligations up 40% to $3.7B support continued subscription growth and margin expansion toward FY2028 consensus EPS of $4.19 [1][6]
key_risks: Memory price normalization: management concedes part of the growth comes from price increases amid a NAND shortage, which could reverse [2]
Valuation: 167x TTM GAAP P/E and an FMP forward PEG of 3.88 leave little room for a guidance miss [5]
Hyperscaler customer concentration and persistent insider selling (zero open-market purchases in 2026) could pressure sentiment [2][7]
